mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases real discount rates and erodes purchasing power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 500K units for six consecutive months indicates a severe housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and reduces overall corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a bifurcated labor market with job creation in lower-wage sectors and layoffs in higher-wage sectors, which compresses wage inflation and reduces corporate profit margins, resulting in flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average by more than 10% signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases reliance on debt and dampens discretionary consumption, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY < 5-year average - 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered months.
